chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Can one pray in the tailyasan (shawl) made by the Magians?' He said, 'Is it not washed with water?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'The new cloth made by the weaver, can I pray in it?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الطَّيْلَسَان: A type of shawl or cloak
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in clothes made by non-Muslims?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that the permissibility of praying in garments made by non-Muslims (Magians) or weavers hinges on the removal of ritual impurity (najasah) through washing with water, reflecting the Shia principle that external contact with impurity does not inherently invalidate the garment unless it remains uncleansed. This ruling clarifies that the origin of the weaver or the newness of the cloth is secondary to the state of purity, distinguishing between mere craftsmanship and ritual cleanliness. The hadith underscores the practical ease in Shia jurisprudence, allowing believers to utilize common market goods without excessive concern for the maker's faith, provided the physical condition of purity is met.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, form Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘The shawl manufactured by the Magian, can one pray Salāt in it?’ Heasws said: ‘Has it not been washed with the water?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘The new cloth worked upon by the weaver, can I pray Salāt in it?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sanaa ‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the shawl made by Zoroastrians if I can perform Salah (prayer) with it. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Can it be washed with water?’ I replied, ‘Yes, it can be washed.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not an offense to perform Salah (prayer) with it.’ I then asked about cloths made by the weavers if I can perform Salah (prayer) with it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so.’”
